title: REMEMBRANCE
mv: Surely he will never be shaken; The righteous will be in everlasting remembrance.
mvp: ‘‘Surely he will never be shaken; The righteous will be in everlasting remembrance.’’ Psalm 112:6 (NKJV)
assignment: List five (5) specific things you want to be remembered for as a Christian (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Most of the time, when we mention the word remembrance, the first thing that comes to our mind is death. However, the remembrance to be examined here is not only about the dead but also the living. Memory is the power of retaining and reproducing mental or sensory impressions. It also means to keep in mind. So, people remember us for what we do and the way we live our lives. History will always have a record of our deeds (positive or negative). Let us make sure we engage in good deeds that will outlive us.
Most of the time, when we remember the following Bible characters, their deeds quickly come to mind.

i: Lot’s Wife: This woman turned into a pillar of salt for looking back during Sodom’s destruction (Genesis 19:15-17; 26). She is remembered for her disobedience and love for the past and worldly things (Luke 17:31-32).
Gehazi: Elisha’s servant, who could have gotten a double portion of Elisha’s anointing, got leprosy because he was covetous (2 Kings 5:20-23; 25-27).
Judas Iscariot: He betrayed his master for money (Matthew 26:14-16; Luke 22:3-6).
Paul: A religious bigot who became an ardent follower of Jesus Christ and gave His all for the service of the Lord (1 Timothy 1:12-16; 1 Corinthians 15:8-10).
Dorcas: A woman full of good works and alms deeds. She gave so much that when she died, the recipients of her largesse looked for Peter to pray for her and bring her back to life (Acts 9:36-43).

b.x: As an individual, what will you be remembered for? We shall examine the following:

i: A Soul Winner: It is a bit difficult to forget how you got born again or the person who led you to Christ. Are you an ardent soul winner? How many people have you brought to Jesus (Proverbs 11:30; John 1:45).

Good Deeds: Good acts are easily remembered consciously or unconsciously (Proverbs 22:9). David remembered the kind deeds of his friend, Jonathan, and summoned his son, Mephibosheth, to the palace to dine with him and restored all his grandfather’s inheritance to him (2 Samuel 9:1; 6-7). Have you done any good deeds lately?
The Righteous: The upright will be remembered for their righteous acts (Proverbs 10:7) because their work will always speak for generations (Psalm 112:1-2). Are you upright in your dealings?

Inventors: History helps us to remember creators and traces a product or idea generated by them (2 Chronicles 26:14-15). What idea have you brought to the table lately? What innovation are you known for?

Labourers: Paul, in Philippians 4:3, mentioned His co-labourers in the work committed into his hand. The harvest is plenty, but the labourers are few (Matthew 9:37). Are you known for your labours or complaints (1 Corinthians 3:9)?

Ground Breakers: Solomon spoke 3,000 proverbs and has 1,500 songs to his credit (1Kings 4:32). Are you a ground breaker? A good team player who is concerned with moving the family, organisation, nation, etc., forward? What price are you willing to pay to be a blessing to humanity?

b.x: What will you be remembered for? Make sure your life counts.

i: Highlight four biblical characters and what they were remembered for.
Mention four possible areas through which people can remember you.
